hints: Work in the coach’s frame. How long does the bullet take to fall 5 m? In that time it must cross the width and also travel the whole length of the coach relative to the coach.
worded:
1. The bullet moves horizontally at u across the track and has no velocity along the track (relative to the ground).

2. From the top corner to the diagonally opposite bottom corner, it must drop 5 m, cross 3 m, and shift 15 m along the coach.

3. Dropping 5 m from zero vertical velocity takes 1 s.

4. Across: 3 m in 1 s gives u = 3 m/s.

5. Along: in the coach’s frame the bullet moves backward at v (the coach moves forward under it). Covering 15 m in 1 s gives v = 15 m/s.
conventional:
![](asset:P000256-sol-1)

Fall of 5 m: $5 = \frac{1}{2}(10)t^{2} \Rightarrow t = 1$ s.

In the coach frame the bullet has velocity $u$ across the coach and $- v$ along it:

$$u = \frac{3}{1} = 3\unit{m/s},\quad\quad v = \frac{15}{1} = 15\unit{m/s}.$$
mistakes: The bullet has no velocity along the track; its apparent motion along the coach is entirely due to the coach moving.
All three displacements happen in the same 1 s fall time.
